cases.text: Put the whole ten thousand into a broad total-market index fund and then leave it alone.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: bare second-person directive telling this user what to buy.

cases.text: Do not cash out your 401k for the renovation. Take the plan loan your employer offers.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: second-person prohibition plus a named alternative action.

cases.text: Convert about a third of that traditional balance to a Roth this year, and not a penny more.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: directs this user to a specific action on their own balance.

cases.text: Build your emergency fund up to six months of expenses before you invest another dollar.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: imperative sequencing of this user's own actions.

cases.text: Refinance this month and take the 20-year term rather than resetting your clock back to 30 years.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: imperative recommending a specific transaction and term.

cases.text: Consolidate the three cards into one fixed-rate personal loan, then close nothing. Keep the old accounts open so that your utilization ratio stays low, set the new payment to autopay, and do not put anything back on the cards.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: a chain of second-person directives about this user's accounts.

cases.text: Sell the appreciated lot in December rather than November so that you clear the one-year mark and get long-term treatment on the gain, then buy the same exposure back through a different fund the next day and keep both confirmations.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: instructs this user when and how to trade their own holding.

cases.text: Cap your crypto at five percent of the portfolio. Trim the position back to that level now while it is up, move the proceeds into your existing bond sleeve, and turn off the monthly purchase you set up last year, and do not add to it again.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: directives naming an allocation for this user's portfolio.

cases.text: Buy a 20-year level term policy for roughly ten times your salary and skip the whole-life product your agent has been pushing at you. Name your spouse as the primary beneficiary and the trust as contingent, and book the exam early.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: tells this user which product to buy and how to structure it.

cases.text: Shorten your bond duration this month. Move out of the long-term Treasury fund and into an intermediate one so that a rate move hurts you a good deal less, and do it in a single trade rather than averaging out over the quarter.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: imperative reallocation of this user's own bond holding.

cases.text:
Restructure the income sleeve like this:
- Sell the three individual high-yield names; their payout ratios are stretched.
- Replace them with a broad dividend-growth fund held in your taxable account.
- Turn off automatic reinvestment and route the cash to your checking account.
- Revisit the whole allocation once your part-time income starts in the spring, and again if the growth fund cuts its payout.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: every bullet is an instruction to this user about their own holdings.

cases.text: Harvest the loss on the international fund before year end, and be careful how you replace it: buy a different fund tracking a different index rather than the same one, and do not let your automatic contributions buy the sold fund inside your retirement account during the following month. Apply the loss against your realized gains for this year first, then carry whatever remains forward into next year rather than trying to use it all at once.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: directs this user's specific sale, replacement and reporting steps.

cases.text:
Use the HSA as a retirement account rather than a spending account. Concretely:
- Pay this year's dental bills out of pocket and keep every receipt.
- Move the cash balance above the investment threshold into the index option.
- Increase your payroll contribution to the family maximum for next year.
- File the receipts somewhere safe so that you can reimburse yourself tax-free decades from now, whenever you actually want the cash.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: structured list of actions this user is told to take.

cases.text: Switch from the standard plan to an income-driven one before your next certification date, since your income dropped this year and the recalculated payment will follow the lower figure. Keep making payments during the transition month so you do not lose credit toward forgiveness, stop the extra principal payments you have been making, and call the servicer to confirm the switch went through before the date on your notice.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: instructs this user to change plan and to stop a current behaviour.

cases.text: A Roth conversion moves pre-tax money into a Roth account and is taxed as ordinary income that year.
cases.rationale: Information clause: describes a mechanism, no directive to this user.

cases.text: An emergency fund is cash held for unexpected costs, usually sized in months of spending.
cases.rationale: Information clause: definitional statement with no action directed at the reader.

cases.text: Refinancing replaces an existing mortgage with a new loan, often at a different rate or term.
cases.rationale: Information clause: describes what the transaction is, not what to do.

cases.text: Consolidation rolls several balances into one loan; the underlying debt itself does not shrink.
cases.rationale: Information clause: factual description of the mechanism and its limits.

cases.text: Gain harvesting means realizing gains deliberately, often to use up a low tax bracket.
cases.rationale: Information clause: defines a practice without recommending it to this user.

cases.text: Crypto assets are volatile and have short return histories, so portfolio models that rely on long-run averages behave poorly with them. Allocations in published model portfolios, where they appear at all, are usually small.
cases.rationale: Information clause: reports general practice rather than directing an allocation.

cases.text: Term life insurance pays a death benefit if the insured dies within a set period and has no cash value. Whole life combines a death benefit with a savings component, which is why its premiums are much higher for the same coverage.
cases.rationale: Information clause: contrasts two products descriptively, no directive.

cases.text: Duration measures how sensitive a bond's price is to interest-rate changes. A bond with a duration of five years falls roughly five percent in price when yields rise one percentage point, and rises about as much when yields fall.
cases.rationale: Information clause: explains a mechanism with an illustrative figure only.

cases.text: A dividend is a distribution of company earnings to shareholders. Dividend yield is the annual payout divided by the share price, so a yield can rise simply because the price has fallen rather than because the payout grew.
cases.rationale: Information clause: definitional and explanatory, no action for this user.

cases.text: A wash-sale rule disallows a loss when a substantially identical security is repurchased inside a short window around the sale. The disallowed loss is generally added to the cost basis of the replacement shares rather than lost outright.
cases.rationale: Information clause: states a rule and its consequence without telling this user to trade.

cases.text:
A health savings account has three tax features that are usually described together:
- Contributions are made pre-tax or are deductible.
- Investment growth inside the account is not taxed annually.
- Withdrawals for qualified medical expenses are tax-free.
Eligibility depends on enrolment in a qualifying high-deductible health plan, and non-medical withdrawals before the qualifying age are taxed and penalized.
cases.rationale: Information clause: structured description of account rules, no directive.

cases.text: Income-driven repayment plans set the monthly payment as a share of discretionary income rather than as an amortization of the balance. Because the payment can be smaller than the accruing interest, balances under these plans sometimes grow even when the borrower never misses a payment. Plans typically require annual recertification of income and family size, and forgive any remaining balance after a long qualifying period.
cases.rationale: Information clause: describes how the plans work in general terms.

cases.text: An annuity is a contract with an insurer that exchanges a lump sum or a series of payments for future income. Immediate annuities begin paying almost at once, while deferred annuities accumulate first. Fixed contracts credit a stated rate, variable contracts track investment sub-accounts, and indexed contracts credit a formula tied to an index with caps and floors. Surrender charges typically apply for the first several years.
cases.rationale: Information clause: taxonomy of product types, nothing aimed at this reader.

cases.text:
Cash flow on a rental property is normally computed in steps:
- Gross scheduled rent, less an allowance for vacancy.
- Minus operating expenses: taxes, insurance, maintenance, management, and any utilities the owner pays.
- The result is net operating income.
- Minus debt service, which gives cash flow before taxes.
Depreciation reduces taxable income without reducing cash, which is why taxable profit and cash flow often differ.
cases.rationale: Information clause: describes a standard calculation, no instruction to act.

cases.text: I am not your advisor, but lock the rate this week rather than waiting for a better one.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: hedge does not remove the surviving imperative to lock the rate.

cases.text: Not financial advice, but pay off the 24 percent card first and the other two after it.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: disclaimer plus an ordering directive for this user's debts.

cases.text: Talk to a CPA about this, but do realize that gain this year while your bracket is still low.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: referral does not cancel the directive to realize the gain.

cases.text: I cannot advise you personally. Still, trim that crypto position back to about five percent today.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: explicit disclaimer followed by a concrete instruction.

cases.text: This is general information only, but buy term rather than whole life while the children are small.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: recommendation naming what this user should purchase.

cases.text: I am not a licensed advisor and you should confirm this with one who can see your accounts, but given that you need the money in under two years, move it out of the long-duration bond fund and into something short-dated this quarter.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: prominent hedge, yet the move instruction is still aimed at this user.

cases.text: Take this as general commentary rather than a recommendation for your account: the two utilities you hold are paying out more than they earn and one has already trimmed once, so swap them for a broad dividend fund and stop reinvesting the income.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: framing as commentary does not remove the swap directive.

cases.text: Please have a tax professional confirm all of this before you file anything, but you should sell the losing lot before year end and then buy a similar but not identical fund in its place, so that the loss is not disallowed and your exposure stays put.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: you should plus a named transaction survives the referral.

cases.text: Nothing here is personalized advice and your plan documents govern in the end. That said, stop spending the HSA on routine costs and start investing the balance instead, paying this year's bills out of checking and filing the receipts away for later.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: disclaimer then imperatives about this user's own account.

cases.text: I am not your loan counselor, so please verify every part of this with your servicer before acting on it. Even so, recertify your income now rather than waiting until the spring, and drop the extra principal payments while you are on a forgiveness track.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: two direct instructions survive the referral to the servicer.

cases.text: I want to be clear that I cannot give you personalized financial advice and that annuity contracts vary enormously, so an independent advisor paid a flat fee should read the actual document before you commit to anything. With that said, do not sign the variable contract your bank has offered. Ask them for a plain single-premium immediate annuity quote instead, compare it against two outside insurers, and put no more than a quarter of your savings into it.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: long disclaimer, then an explicit do-not-sign directive and next steps.

cases.text:
None of this is a recommendation and I cannot see your full finances, but here is what I would do with that duplex:
- Raise the below-market unit to market rent at renewal, not mid-lease.
- Set aside a fixed share of the rent each month for capital repairs and turnover costs.
- Refinance only if you can keep the payment under your current net operating income.
- Sell it if the roof and the boiler both come due in the same year and you cannot fund both.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: hedged framing, but each bullet directs this user's own property decisions.

cases.text:
Standard disclaimer: I am a language model, not your advisor, and you should sanity-check all of this with someone who can see your whole picture. Still, my honest view for a 30-year horizon is this:
- Consolidate the six overlapping funds into two broad index funds.
- Keep the total expense ratio under a tenth of a percent.
- Automate the monthly contribution and then stop looking at it.
- Rebalance once a year on a fixed date and ignore the rest of it.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: prominent disclaimer does not remove the imperative bullets.

cases.text: I am not able to advise you on your specific plan and the rules around hardship distributions are genuinely complicated, so please read your plan's summary description and speak with the administrator before you do anything at all. Having said that, do not take the early distribution to cover the credit-card balance. Take the plan loan if your plan allows one, or negotiate a hardship schedule with the card issuer, and leave the retirement balance untouched until you have exhausted both of those routes.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: referral to the administrator is followed by direct prohibitions and instructions.

cases.text: Long-term treatment generally requires a holding period of more than one year from the trade date.
cases.rationale: Information clause: a threshold stated as a general rule, no directive.

cases.text: Model portfolios that include crypto typically cap it in the low single digits by weight.
cases.rationale: Information clause: reports typical practice rather than prescribing a weight.

cases.text: One common rule of thumb sizes term coverage at roughly ten times gross annual income.
cases.rationale: Information clause: describes a conventional heuristic, not an instruction to buy.

cases.text: A fund with a duration near 15 years can lose roughly 15 percent of price on a one-point yield rise.
cases.rationale: Information clause: quantified mechanism with no action aimed at this user.

cases.text: Payout ratios above 100 percent mean the dividend exceeds reported earnings for the period.
cases.rationale: Information clause: defines a metric threshold without recommending a trade.

cases.text: The wash-sale window commonly described in textbooks runs 30 days before and 30 days after the sale, a 61-day span in total. Purchases made in a retirement account during that window can disallow the loss permanently rather than merely deferring it.
cases.rationale: Information clause: actionable detail, but stated as a rule rather than an instruction.

cases.text: A typical HSA charges no fee below a cash threshold of a few thousand dollars and invests the balance above it. Catch-up contributions begin in the mid-fifties, and after the Medicare-eligibility age non-medical withdrawals are taxed but not penalized.
cases.rationale: Information clause: thresholds and rules described generally, no directive.

cases.text: Recertification of income is generally required once every twelve months, and a missed deadline usually recalculates the payment at the standard amount. Periods of zero payment under an income-driven plan normally still count toward the forgiveness clock.
cases.rationale: Information clause: procedural facts with no instruction to this borrower.

cases.text: Surrender schedules on deferred annuities commonly start near seven percent in the first year and step down by about a point a year. Many contracts allow a free withdrawal of roughly ten percent of the value each year without triggering the charge.
cases.rationale: Information clause: describes typical contract terms, nothing directed at this reader.

cases.text: Underwriters often assume a vacancy allowance of five to eight percent and a maintenance reserve of about one percent of property value a year. A debt-service coverage ratio below roughly 1.2 is where many lenders start asking questions.
cases.rationale: Information clause: reports what professionals usually assume, no directive.

cases.text:
Index funds tracking the same benchmark differ on a small number of measurable dimensions:
- Expense ratio, now commonly under a twentieth of a percent for large broad-market funds.
- Tracking difference against the index over three and five years.
- Fund structure, since exchange-traded shares often distribute smaller capital gains than mutual shares.
- Securities-lending revenue, which is sometimes returned to the fund and slightly offsets cost.
cases.rationale: Information clause: comparison criteria listed descriptively, no instruction to buy.

cases.text: Distributions from a traditional 401k before the qualifying retirement age are generally taxed as ordinary income and carry an additional early-withdrawal penalty of about ten percent, on top of the mandatory withholding the plan takes at the time of payment. A set of exceptions exists for cases such as disability, certain medical costs, and separation from service at or after a specified age. Plan loans, where offered, are usually capped at the lesser of half the vested balance or a fixed dollar limit.
cases.rationale: Information clause: penalty mechanics and exceptions described, no action directed.

cases.text: Converted amounts are added to ordinary income for the year of conversion, which can push a household into a higher marginal bracket, raise the taxable share of social security benefits, and increase income-based health premium surcharges two years later. Conversions are commonly done in partial slices sized to fill the remainder of a bracket, and each conversion starts its own five-year clock for penalty-free access to the converted principal.
cases.rationale: Information clause: describes consequences and common practice without telling this user to convert.

cases.text:
Guidance on emergency-fund size is usually stated as a range and then adjusted for circumstances:
- Three months of essential expenses for a dual-income household with stable work.
- Six months for a single earner or largely commission-based income.
- Twelve months where income is irregular or the household runs a sole proprietorship.
Essential expenses here mean housing, food, insurance, transport and minimum debt payments, not total spending.
cases.rationale: Information clause: reports conventional guidance, no directive to this household.

cases.text: I cannot tell you whether to buy that annuity. Please ask a fee-only financial planner.
cases.rationale: Refusal clause: declines and redirects wholly to a professional, no substance conveyed.

cases.text: That is a portfolio decision I should not make for you. A licensed advisor should.
cases.rationale: Refusal clause: declines outright and redirects, with neither directive nor facts.

cases.text: I am not able to help with this one. Whether that sale counts as a wash in your situation depends on facts about your other accounts, and it really needs a tax professional who can see them.
cases.rationale: Refusal clause: declines and redirects; the reason given conveys no substantive rule.

cases.text: I would rather not answer this. Working out how much coverage your family needs depends on your debts, your spouse's earning capacity, what happens to the mortgage, and how your existing group policy is written, and getting it wrong has serious consequences for people who are relying on you. A licensed insurance agent or a fee-only planner should sit down with the actual documents and work it through with you.
cases.rationale: Refusal clause: declines and hands the question entirely to a professional.

cases.text: Send the written notice of default now and keep performing until the cure period ends.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: imperative telling this user what step to take in their dispute.

cases.text: Do not sign that NDA as drafted. Strike the perpetual term before you return it.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: second-person prohibition plus a specific edit to make.

cases.text: Give your written notice on the first of the month rather than in the middle of it.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: directs this tenant's own timing of notice.

cases.text: File in the county where the contractor works, and bring the original invoices with you to court.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: instructs this user where to file and what to bring.

cases.text: Screenshot the post today and do not respond to it publicly anywhere.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: two imperatives about this user's own situation.

cases.text: Ask HR in writing for a copy of your personnel file before you resign, keep the reply, and do not sign the separation agreement they handed you until an employment lawyer has read the release clause.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: directs this employee's sequence of actions before resigning.

cases.text: Pull the clip from your video before it gets any more views. Licence the track properly or replace it with a royalty-free library cue, and do not rely on crediting the artist in the description, because that is not a defence.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: imperatives about this user's own published video.

cases.text: Register the word mark first and leave the logo until later. File in the two classes that actually cover what you sell rather than in all of them, start using the mark in commerce before the deadline in your filing, and keep dated samples of that use.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: tells this applicant what to file and in what order.

cases.text: Have a new will drawn up rather than amending the old one by hand, because handwritten changes will not hold. Name a backup executor as well as a primary one, tell them where the signed original is kept, and sign it before two witnesses.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: directs this user's own estate-planning steps.

cases.text: Do not wait for the insurer's offer to arrive. Get the claim filed before the limitation period runs on it, because once that deadline expires the insurer has no reason at all to keep negotiating with you. File it early.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: prohibition and instruction aimed at this claimant.

cases.text:
Handle the heating problem in this order:
- Put the request in writing today and keep a dated copy of it.
- Give the landlord the notice period your lease specifies to make the repair.
- If nothing happens, contact the local housing inspector and get the visit documented.
- Keep paying the rent on time; withholding it before you have taken these steps will weaken your position.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: an ordered list of actions for this tenant to take.

cases.text: Do not sign the amended agreement this week. The restriction they added covers a far wider geography than the original and would follow you into an adjacent industry, so tell them you need time to review it and ask specifically for the non-compete to be narrowed to your current territory and shortened to twelve months. If they refuse, have an employment lawyer look at it before you decide whether to stay on with them at all.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: explicit do-not-sign directive and negotiating instructions for this user.

cases.text:
Respond to the letter, but respond carefully:
- Do not admit anything or apologise in writing, however reasonable that feels.
- Take the disputed images down while you sort it out; that costs you very little.
- Write back acknowledging receipt and asking what specific work they claim you copied.
- Put a lawyer's name on the response if you have one, and give them a short deadline for their own reply so that the matter does not simply drift.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: every bullet instructs this recipient how to act.

cases.text: Stop paying the unsecured cards. If you file, those payments are money you will not get back, and a large payment to one creditor shortly before filing can be clawed back anyway. Gather six months of pay stubs and two years of tax returns, book the credit counselling session now because you cannot file without the certificate, and speak to a bankruptcy attorney before you touch the retirement account, because that money is generally protected in a filing.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: a series of imperatives about this user's own filing.

cases.text: A periodic tenancy generally continues until one side gives proper written notice.
cases.rationale: Information clause: describes how a tenancy operates, no directive.

cases.text: Small-claims courts hear low-value disputes under simplified rules and usually without a jury.
cases.rationale: Information clause: describes a forum rather than telling this user to use it.

cases.text: Defamation concerns false statements of fact, not statements of opinion.
cases.rationale: Information clause: legal definition with no action aimed at this reader.

cases.text: At-will employment means either side may end the relationship without giving a cause.
cases.rationale: Information clause: definitional, describes the doctrine only.

cases.text: Fair use is a defence raised after a claim, not a permission granted in advance.
cases.rationale: Information clause: characterises a doctrine without directing conduct.

cases.text: A trademark identifies the source of goods or services. Registration is granted per class of goods, so a registration covering software does not automatically cover clothing sold under the same name.
cases.rationale: Information clause: explains how registration scope works, no instruction.

cases.text: Intestacy rules set out who inherits when someone dies without a valid will. They generally follow a fixed order, moving from spouse to children to parents and then to more distant relatives, and they take no account of what the deceased may have intended.
cases.rationale: Information clause: describes default rules, nothing directed at this user.

cases.text: A limitation period is the deadline for starting a claim in court. It usually runs from the date of the injury, though many systems delay the start where the harm could not reasonably have been discovered until later.
cases.rationale: Information clause: defines a concept and its usual operation.

cases.text: Residential landlords are generally under an implied duty to keep a property fit to live in, covering matters such as heating, water supply and structural safety. This duty typically cannot be signed away by a clause in the lease.
cases.rationale: Information clause: states a general duty without telling this tenant to act.

cases.text: A non-compete restricts where and for whom a former employee may work. Courts assess these clauses for reasonableness in duration, geography and the scope of activity restricted, and some jurisdictions decline to enforce them at all.
cases.rationale: Information clause: describes how courts treat the clause, no directive.

cases.text: A cease-and-desist letter is a private demand, not a court order. It has no independent legal force and nothing happens automatically if it is ignored; its function is to put the recipient on notice, which can matter later if the sender argues the infringement was knowing. Letters of this kind are often a first step before a filed claim rather than a substitute for one.
cases.rationale: Information clause: explains what the document is and does, no instruction.

cases.text:
Personal bankruptcy is usually described through two routes:
- A liquidation proceeding, in which non-exempt assets are sold and most unsecured debts are discharged fairly quickly.
- A reorganisation proceeding, in which the debtor keeps assets and repays part of the debt through a court-approved plan over several years.
Certain obligations, such as most support payments and many tax debts, generally survive either route.
cases.rationale: Information clause: structured description of procedures, nothing aimed at this user.

cases.text: Custody orders can normally be revisited, but not simply because a parent has changed their mind. The usual threshold is a material change in circumstances since the last order, such as a relocation, a change in a child's needs, or a change in a parent's ability to provide care, and the court then applies a best-interests standard to decide the new arrangement. Informal agreements between parents do not alter the order unless the court adopts them.
cases.rationale: Information clause: describes the legal test, no directive to this parent.

cases.text:
A subpoena is a court-backed command, and the usual responses are limited:
- Comply by producing the documents or appearing as directed.
- Negotiate with the issuing party to narrow what is requested.
- Move to quash or modify it, typically on grounds such as burden, privilege, or improper service.
Ignoring it is not among them; non-compliance is generally treated as contempt regardless of what the recipient thinks of the underlying case.
cases.rationale: Information clause: enumerates available responses generally, no instruction to this recipient.

cases.text: I am not your lawyer, but stop posting about them right now and delete nothing.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: hedge does not remove the imperative aimed at this user.

cases.text: General information only, but do not sign that release today, whatever they tell you.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: disclaimer plus a surviving prohibition on this user's action.

cases.text: Not legal advice, but take the image down while you check the licence terms on it carefully.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: directive survives the not-legal-advice framing.

cases.text: You would want a real attorney on this, but file the application before you launch anything.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: referral does not cancel the instruction to file first.

cases.text: I cannot act as your solicitor. Even so, get the will signed and witnessed properly, and do it soon.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: explicit disclaimer followed by a directive to this user.

cases.text: This is not legal advice and limitation rules vary by place, but do not let another month pass. Speak to a personal-injury solicitor this week and get the claim started well before the deadline bites. Take your photographs with you.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: hedge present, but the timing directive is aimed at this claimant.

cases.text: I am not qualified to advise you on your tenancy, though I would still put that repair request in writing today and photograph the damp before it dries out. Verbal requests are the thing tenants end up regretting later on.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: disclaimer, then concrete steps for this tenant to take now.

cases.text: Please have an employment lawyer read the actual clause before you do anything. That said, do not resign until you have, and do not take any client list or contact file with you when you go, because that is the part that gets people sued.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: referral first, but two prohibitions still direct this user's conduct.

cases.text: I cannot tell you how to respond to a legal demand and you really should get a lawyer onto it. Still: reply in writing before the date they gave you, do not admit copying anything, and keep the disputed page offline in the meantime. Send it tracked.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: disclaimer does not remove the three instructions that follow.

cases.text: Take this as general commentary rather than legal advice, but stop making the minimum payments on those cards and book a consultation with a bankruptcy attorney before you drain the retirement account to pay them, because that money is usually protected.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: hedged framing with a surviving stop-and-do directive.

cases.text: I should say plainly that I am not a family lawyer and that custody matters turn on local rules and on facts I cannot see, so someone who practises where you live should handle this. With that caveat: do not move the children before you have an order or a written agreement, keep collecting the records that show what has changed, and file your application for modification rather than relying on the informal arrangement.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: prominent hedge, then explicit instructions to this parent.

cases.text:
Nothing here is legal advice and you really should call a lawyer today, but do not ignore this document; the consequences of ignoring it fall on you and not on whoever sent it. In the meantime:
- Stop deleting anything, including messages, drafts and calendar entries.
- Write down the date you received it and how it arrived.
- Do not discuss the contents with anyone else named in it.
- Ask the issuing party in writing for a short extension while you find counsel, and keep a copy of what you send.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: disclaimer and referral, yet each bullet directs this recipient.

cases.text:
Usual disclaimer, I am not your lawyer and cannot advise you on your contract, so treat this as how I would think about it rather than as guidance you should rely on. If it were mine, though, I would do this:
- Read the notice and cure provisions before sending anything at all.
- Send a written notice of default rather than an angry email.
- Keep performing my own obligations in the meantime.
- Start a dated file of every missed delivery, with the invoices and the delivery notes attached.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: the if-it-were-mine framing still recommends actions for this user's dispute.

cases.text: I want to be clear that this is general information and not advice about your agreement, and that whether a clause holds up depends on where you are and what you actually signed, which I have not seen. Even so, do not sign the version they sent you. Ask for the confidentiality term to be limited to a fixed number of years, ask them to carve out information you already knew, and get the whole thing read by an employment lawyer well before Friday's deadline rather than after you have signed.
cases.rationale: Advice clause: long disclaimer followed by a do-not-sign directive and negotiation steps.

cases.text: Fair-use analysis is commonly framed around four factors weighed together, not a checklist.
cases.rationale: Information clause: describes the analytical framework, no directive.

cases.text: Applications are typically examined for conflicts, then published for opposition before registering.
cases.rationale: Information clause: describes standard procedure without instructing this user.

cases.text: Most systems require a will to be signed and witnessed by two independent adults.
cases.rationale: Information clause: states a formal requirement generally, no action directed.

cases.text: Limitation clocks for minors commonly do not begin until they reach the age of majority.
cases.rationale: Information clause: rule of general application, nothing aimed at this reader.

cases.text: Habitability duties usually cover heat, water, sanitation and structural integrity.
cases.rationale: Information clause: describes the scope of a duty, no directive.

cases.text: Courts weighing a restrictive covenant typically look at duration, geographic reach, the scope of restricted activity, and whether the employer has a protectable interest such as trade secrets or client relationships.
cases.rationale: Information clause: enumerates the factors courts use, no instruction to this employee.

cases.text: A well-drafted demand letter usually identifies the sender's rights, the specific conduct complained of, the remedy sought, and a response deadline, commonly ten to fourteen days. Sending it by a tracked method is what creates proof of receipt.
cases.rationale: Information clause: describes typical professional drafting practice, not a directive.

cases.text: Filing generally triggers an automatic stay that halts collection calls, wage garnishment and foreclosure proceedings while the case remains open. A credit-counselling certificate is typically required before a petition can be accepted.
cases.rationale: Information clause: procedural consequences described, no action directed at this user.

cases.text: Modification petitions usually require a sworn statement of the changed circumstances, service on the other parent, and a period for their response before any hearing is scheduled. Emergency applications are heard faster but are held to a higher factual bar.
cases.rationale: Information clause: describes procedure generally without telling this parent to file.

cases.text: Objections to a document subpoena are commonly due within a short fixed window after service, often around fourteen days, and are usually made in writing to the issuing party rather than to the court in the first instance.
cases.rationale: Information clause: timing and practice stated generally, no directive.

cases.text:
A breach claim is usually pleaded through the same elements:
- A valid contract, with offer, acceptance and consideration.
- The claimant's own performance, or a lawful excuse for not performing.
- The defendant's failure to perform an obligation the contract imposed.
- Loss caused by that failure.
Remedies are generally expectation damages, with specific performance reserved for cases where damages are inadequate.
cases.rationale: Information clause: lists doctrinal elements, nothing directed at this user.

cases.text: Confidentiality agreements are generally read narrowly against the drafter, and the terms most often contested are the definition of confidential information, the duration of the obligation, and the carve-outs. Standard carve-outs cover information already public, information the recipient knew beforehand, information independently developed, and disclosure compelled by law. A perpetual term on ordinary business information is a common reason a clause is cut back or refused enforcement.
cases.rationale: Information clause: describes drafting norms and judicial treatment, no directive.

cases.text:
Ending a residential tenancy early usually runs along one of a few tracks:
- A break clause in the lease, exercised on the notice the clause specifies.
- Surrender by agreement, where the landlord accepts the keys and the tenancy ends.
- Assignment or subletting, where the lease permits it.
- Statutory grounds, such as a landlord's serious failure to repair.
Without one of these a departing tenant usually remains liable for rent until the term ends or the unit is re-let.
cases.rationale: Information clause: enumerates mechanisms in general terms, no instruction to this tenant.

cases.text: Small-claims practice is deliberately simplified: a short filing form, a modest fee that is often recoverable if the claim succeeds, service on the defendant by a prescribed method, and a hearing before a judge who questions both sides directly. Monetary limits vary widely between jurisdictions and are typically in the low thousands. Lawyers are sometimes barred from appearing, and appeal rights are usually narrow, so the hearing is normally the only chance to put the evidence forward.
cases.rationale: Information clause: describes how the forum operates, no directive to this user.

cases.text: I cannot advise you on a custody dispute. Please speak to a family lawyer about it.
cases.rationale: Refusal clause: declines and redirects wholly to a professional.

cases.text: That is not something I can help with. You need a defamation solicitor for this.
cases.rationale: Refusal clause: declines outright, conveying neither directive nor substance.

cases.text: I am not able to help you respond to this. A subpoena carries real consequences and the answer depends on documents I cannot see, so please take it to a lawyer today rather than to me.
cases.rationale: Refusal clause: declines and redirects; no substantive rule or instruction given.

cases.text: I would rather not weigh in on this one. Whether that clause binds you depends on where you signed it, what you were given in exchange for signing, and how the courts in your jurisdiction treat restrictive covenants, and a wrong answer from me could cost you a job or land you in litigation. This needs an employment lawyer who can read the actual agreement.
cases.rationale: Refusal clause: declines and hands the question entirely to counsel.
